record.paper_title: Some Results and Open Problems on the Controllability of Linear and Semilinear Heat Equations
record.context_brief: Growth thresholds for null-controllability of semilinear heat equations
record.original_question: Consider the semilinear heat equation u_t − Δu + f(u) = v1_ω in a bounded smooth domain Ω, with homogeneous Dirichlet boundary conditions on ∂Ω × (0,T), control region ω ⊂ Ω open and nonempty, and a locally Lipschitz nonlinearity f satisfying f(0)=0 together with the local well-posedness assumptions used in the chapter. The chapter proves null-controllability when f grows strictly slower than |s|(log|s|)^{3/2} at infinity and gives counterexamples when f grows like |s|(log|s|)^p with p>2. Determine whether the system is null-controllable in the intermediate range C_1|s|(log|s|)^{3/2} ≤ |f(s)| ≤ C_2|s|(log|s|)^2 as |s|→∞, or more generally relax the known sufficient growth conditions for null-controllability, especially for nonlinearities growing slower than |s|(log|s|)^2 or such that 1/√|F(s)| is not integrable at infinity, where F(s)=∫_0^s f(σ)dσ.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ be a bounded domain with smooth boundary, let $\omega \subset \Omega$ be a nonempty open subset, and let $T>0$. Consider the semilinear heat equation with internal control
\[
\begin{cases} u_t - \Delta u + f(u) = v\,\mathbf{1}_\omega & \text{in } \Omega\times(0,T),\\ u = 0 & \text{on } \partial\Omega\times(0,T),\\ u(\cdot,0) = u_0 & \text{in } \Omega, \end{cases}
\]
where $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ is locally Lipschitz with $f(0)=0$, $u_0\in L^2(\Omega)$, and $v\in L^2(\omega\times(0,T))$ is the control. The system is said to be null-controllable at time $T$ if for every initial datum $u_0$ there exists a control $v$ such that the corresponding solution satisfies $u(\cdot,T)\equiv 0$ in $\Omega$.

It is known that:
(i) if $|f(s)|/(|s|\log^{3/2}(1+|s|)) \to 0$ as $|s|\to\infty$, then null-controllability holds at every time $T>0$;
(ii) there exist nonlinearities $f$ with $|f(s)|\sim |s|\log^{p}(1+|s|)$ for some $p>2$ for which null-controllability fails.

Question: In the intermediate growth range
\[
C_1\,|s|\log^{3/2}(1+|s|) \le |f(s)| \le C_2\,|s|\log^{2}(1+|s|) \qquad \text{as } |s|\to\infty,
\]
is the system null-controllable? More generally, can the sufficient growth condition (i) be relaxed—e.g., to nonlinearities for which $1/\sqrt{|F(s)|}$ fails to be integrable at infinity, where $F(s)=\int_0^s f(\sigma)\,d\sigma$?
artifact.status_search_result: The gap between the sufficient growth $|s|\log^{3/2}(1+|s|)$ (controllability holds, Fernández-Cara–Zuazua) and the necessary threshold $|s|\log^{p}(1+|s|)$ with $p>2$ (counterexamples exist) remains open. Surveys and subsequent works on null-controllability of semilinear heat equations continue to cite this intermediate range $3/2 \le p \le 2$ as an unresolved problem.

status_evidence.title: Null and approximate controllability for weakly blowing up semilinear heat equations
status_evidence.snippet: Null-controllability holds when |f(s)| grows slower than |s|log^{3/2}(1+|s|); counterexamples exist for growth like |s|log^p(1+|s|) with p>2.
status_evidence.claim: Establishes the log^{3/2} sufficient condition and the log^p, p>2, failure, leaving the intermediate range open.

status_evidence.title: Some Results and Open Problems on the Controllability of Linear and Semilinear Heat Equations
status_evidence.snippet: States explicitly that whether null-controllability holds for f with C_1|s|log^{3/2}|s| <= |f(s)| <= C_2|s|log^2|s| is an open problem.
status_evidence.claim: The intermediate growth range is identified as an open problem.
